lead: The ANC is settling on case-by-case coalition deals after its local election slump, with eThekwini still without a majority partner as MK leads on 86 seats. Severe storms are forecast for western KZN today, and the rand heads into CPI and a SARB rate decision near R17/$.

items.title: ANC opts for flexible, council-by-council coalition approach
items.summary: Sources say the ANC's NEC will judge municipal pacts on local conditions, treating the DA as a last-resort partner. The NEC reportedly did not call for Ramaphosa to step down despite the poor result.

items.title: eThekwini still hung: MK holds 86 of 223 seats as talks continue
items.summary: No party reached the 112 seats needed. MK leads, followed by the DA on 57, ANC 37 and IFP 15. An ANC-DA-IFP bloc would fall just short and need smaller parties; MK has given mixed signals on talking to the DA.

items.title: Level 5 storm warning for western KZN and parts of six provinces
items.summary: The Weather Service warned of severe thunderstorms over western KwaZulu-Natal, the far eastern Free State and Mpumalanga Highveld, with possible flooding and power and communication disruptions. Eastern KZN faced a disruptive-rain alert.

items.title: Mantashe warns split black vote is eroding the ANC
items.summary: The ANC chair said fragmentation could destroy the party, which slid to about 30% in the local polls from 45% in 2024. The SACP welcomed the ANC's stance of partnering with the DA only as a last resort.

items.title: Treasury to keep withholding funds from poorly run councils
items.summary: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said cutting transfers will remain a tool to force better performance. Treasury froze equitable-share payments to 69 municipalities in July, later releasing R7.1bn to 49 of them.

items.title: Pappas sworn in for second term as uMngeni mayor
items.summary: Chris Pappas pledged to prioritise basic services in the Midlands municipality, including refuse collection, potholes and streetlights, and set a target of supporting 2,000 net new jobs.

items.title: Defence witness flags red flags in SANDF contract at Mapisa-Nqakula trial
items.summary: A retired intelligence general told the Pretoria High Court he spotted warning signs in the Umkhombe Marine repatriation deal before it was awarded. The former minister denies all corruption and money laundering charges; the case resumes Monday.

items.title: Presidency rebukes Nigerian envoy over social media conduct
items.summary: The Presidency called High Commissioner Femi Fani-Kayode's online behaviour grossly inappropriate. He arrived in South Africa on 25 October amid strained ties over attacks on foreign nationals.

items.title: Iran says tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz; UN urges halt to ship attacks
items.summary: Iran's navy said a tanker struck a mine and caught fire, which Tehran called the fourth such incident in 24 hours. Separately, Qatar and Turkiye signed a mutual defence pact.

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit in China
items.summary: The White House said the leaders will meet in Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of APEC, with the Iran war and nuclear arsenals on the agenda. US officials played down hopes of a deal.

items.title: US flights still disrupted after nationwide ground stop
items.summary: A telecoms outage at regional air traffic centres led the FAA to halt departures for over four hours on Friday. Thousands of flights were cancelled and airlines warned recovery could take days.

items.title: Sudan's army gains ground in Kordofan against RSF
items.summary: The SAF took the West Kordofan town of al-Khuwai after breaking the RSF siege of al-Obeid. The RSF still controls all five Darfur states in a war that has displaced more than 14 million.

items.title: South Sudan delays first national elections to February
items.summary: The election commission moved the vote from 22 December to 11 February 2027, at least the third postponement. Voter registration runs until 28 November.

items.title: Rand slips to seven-month low near R17 ahead of CPI and SARB
items.summary: The rand weakened about 1.2% on Friday to roughly 16.98 per dollar after hot US producer inflation fed Fed hike bets; the Top-40 fell about 0.7%. October CPI and the SARB rate decision are due this week.

items.title: December outlook: petrol cut, diesel hike as levy relief shrinks
items.summary: Mid-month CEF data pointed to inland 95 petrol falling about R1.82 a litre and 500ppm diesel rising about R1.49, as the temporary fuel levy cut is reduced on 1 December. The rand's slide since could trim the petrol relief.

items.title: Standard Bank hit with R17m penalty over anti-money-laundering gaps
items.summary: The Prudential Authority sanctioned the bank after an inspection found weak customer checks and missing records. R5m of the penalty is suspended, leaving R12m payable.

items.title: Springboks fall 21-19 to France in Paris despite comeback
items.summary: South Africa trailed 21-7 at half-time and scored three second-half tries, but a missed conversion left them two points short in the Nations Championship clash on Friday.

items.title: Bafana held 2-2 by Kenya after late equaliser
items.summary: Relebohile Mofokeng put South Africa ahead in Soweto before Kenya levelled late. Bafana lead their AFCON qualifying group on seven points, with Guinea one behind, and face Kenya in Nairobi on Tuesday.

items.title: Proteas open two-Test series against Bangladesh at the Wanderers
items.summary: The first Test starts this morning in Johannesburg, with captain Temba Bavuma urging a ruthless approach.

items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: Huang left both the CEO role and the board after 33 years amid personal and conflict-of-interest allegations. Shares dropped more than 14% at one point, and the board is searching for a permanent successor.
